title: Process dynamics
physicalPurpose: Compare a real held-input heater response with the prior PI record.
objective: Record the actual 75% to 85% held-input response and distinguish it from a PI-controlled trace.

simplifications: First-order heater with gain 0.2, time constant 5 s and one-second input delay
The simulator starts at 35 degC with 75 percent delayed-input history
PI is inactive during this prepared open-loop record

baseline.limitation: The prior PI record contains controller movement and is not the heater response alone.

change.decision: Use the recorded applied command and PV trace to compare the held-input response with the prior PI result.

abortPredicates: Temperature is nonfinite or leaves 33-39 degC
safety.restorationMode: Normal completion, abort or disabled authority command zero heat; restart the simulator to restore 35 degC and 75 percent delayed-input history.
simulationOnlyRestrictions: The held-input record is simulation evidence for this lesson model.

video.viewerOutcome: Compare the held 85 percent record with the prior PI response.

learning.context: A real held 85 percent command is applied to the supplied heater after its 35 degC, 75 percent history.
learning.reason: A PI record changes its command while temperature moves, so it does not isolate the heater response.
theory: Process gain is the settled temperature change divided by the applied command change.
The supplied heater has gain 0.2 degC per percentage point, time constant 5 s and one-second delay.
The trace is observed evidence; ST must not replace it with a calculated equilibrium.
learning.workedPrediction: Predict no PV motion before the one-second delay, about 36.264 degC at 6 s and 36.986 degC at 26 s.
practicalPreparation: Confirm the 35 degC initial state and 75 percent delayed-input history.
Start the declared observation and record applied command and measured temperature for 30 s.
learning.baseline: Use the prior PI result as the controller-plus-process comparison record.
learning.change: The prepared project holds 85 percent with PI inactive.
learning.comparison: Compare the applied-command history and PV trace, rather than treating PI settling time as a heater time constant.
learning.validation: Check the delay, gradual approach and bounded command/PV values in the saved held-input record.
learning.explanation: The observed response supports the next physical model discussion without claiming that a computed equilibrium is measured evidence.
learning.transfer: Energy balance next derives the heater relationship from stored energy and heat loss.
